first_impression.reaction: I went to the FAQ first, like I always do. The answers point to real bodies (the Junta Central Electoral, the Attorney-General's Department, the National Hurricane Center) and have dates on them, so I went back up and read the rest. It reads like research, not a brochure. Then I got to the end and there's nothing on what the Advisor costs or how you get paid. What's the catch?

journey.quote: As at November 2026; this is general information, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Good. It's dated and it doesn't pretend to be a lawyer. That's how I'd want it written.

journey.section: Getting legally married in the Dominican Republic or holding a symbolic ceremony
journey.quote: Which of these the Dominican registry accepts is a question to check with the Dominican authorities before you order anything.
journey.reaction: They admit they don't know rather than guessing. I'll take that over a confident wrong answer.

journey.section: The civil judge, witnesses and the day itself
journey.quote: The consulate's list also names padrinos, a minimum of one, alongside two witnesses.
journey.reaction: It points out that the two official sources don't match and tells me to ask. Honest about where the information runs out.

journey.section: When to plan a Punta Cana wedding
journey.quote: They are averages for the 30 years from 1961 to 1990, and a rain day is a day with at least 1 mm of rain.
journey.reaction: Real numbers with a source and a definition, which is what I want. But 1961 to 1990 is old data, and the sentence before calls it 'a clear picture of the year'. Say it's a long-run average and leave it there.

journey.section: Getting your guests to Punta Cana from Australia
journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller's advice for the Dominican Republic is to exercise a high degree of caution, due to the threat of violent crime.
journey.reaction: A travel business putting the bad news in plainly. Not many would. That gets my trust more than anything else on the page.

journey.section: Legal at home, symbolic in Punta Cana
journey.quote: You can sign the legal papers at home with a celebrant, then hold a ceremony in Punta Cana that carries all the meaning and none of the paperwork.
journey.reaction: This is where it goes soft and starts selling. 'All the meaning' is filler. Just tell me there's no Dominican paperwork.

journey.quote: Ask how many weddings the property holds on your date, and whether any share your ceremony site, reception space or photo spots.
journey.reaction: Useful. These are the questions I'd put in my spreadsheet. Nobody's selling me a resort here.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, and works in your time zone with quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: Quotes in AUD from who, and with what on top? If the resort's price comes through you, I need to know whether you take a cut. This is the one line about the service, and it doesn't answer the only question I have about it.

journey.quote: Compare them line by line, ask what happens to the space if another wedding is booked that day, and get every inclusion in writing.
journey.reaction: Fair advice. It would be more useful if it also told me to get each item priced on its own, so a package can't hide what I'm paying for.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor works with you from start to finish, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: Fine, but what does that cost me and what does it actually cover? There's no fee model on the page, no example budget and no real reviews. I'm not getting on a call just to find out the price.

unanswered_questions: What does Wedded Concierge or a Wedded Advisor cost? Is it a flat fee, a percentage, or nothing up front?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or put a mark-up on resort or supplier prices?
When the Advisor gives me 'quotes in AUD', are those the resort's own prices converted, or prices with a margin added?
What exactly does the Advisor do, and what's left to me? The page says the registry booking is my job, but not what you handle.
Is there a real Punta Cana wedding with its actual budget I can look at?
Where can I read independent reviews of Wedded Wonderland?

turn_offs_found.quote: You can sign the legal papers at home with a celebrant, then hold a ceremony in Punta Cana that carries all the meaning and none of the paperwork.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional wording in an otherwise factual guide. It doesn't tell me anything.

turn_offs_found.quote: Punta Cana tends to arrive on the shortlist through a photograph: white chairs, pale sand, water the colour of glass.
turn_offs_found.why: Mood-setting in the intro. Mild, and the next sentence gets to the point, so I let it go.

turn_offs_found.quote: The World Meteorological Organization's climate normals for Punta Cana, supplied by the Dominican national weather service ONAMET, give a clear picture of the year.
turn_offs_found.why: Averages from 1961 to 1990 aren't 'a clear picture'. It oversells data that is honestly presented everywhere else.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the legal and hurricane sections

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, begin with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: The CTAs come after the evidence, not before, and that's right. But I enquire once my main questions are answered on the page, and the main one, what you charge and whether you take a cut from the venue, isn't answered. I'd go and check your site for a fee page first. If it's not there, you're off the list.
